category.text: $module$/top/期末試験_English のデフォルト

info.text: Information Literacy Final Exam (English draft translation)

questiontext.text: In the DIKW model, which of the following is the most appropriate description of "Information"?

generalfeedback.text: DIKW consists of four stages: data, information, knowledge, and wisdom. A describes "data," C describes "knowledge," and D describes "wisdom," so they are incorrect. One aspect of information literacy is the skill of converting this data into information and knowledge.

answer.text: Objective facts and the like, in an unorganized state
Data that has been organized and analyzed according to some criterion so that it can be interpreted
A state in which information has been compiled, systematized, and structured
A state in which knowledge has been correctly understood and turned into values and morals

name.text: Q_コミュニケーション_AからB (EN)

questiontext.text: When a person A conveys information to another person B, which of the following is the most appropriate description of how it is "transmitted"?

generalfeedback.text: Communication is a process in which "the sender encodes, it passes through a medium, and the receiver reconstructs," so "having sent" does not necessarily mean "having conveyed." That is precisely why one must make an effort to communicate from the other party's perspective.

answer.text: As long as information passes through a medium (radio waves, paper, sound, etc.), it is conveyed to B with 100% identical meaning, exactly as A intended.
The receiver B merely takes in the signs as they are and does not perform any interpretation or reconstruction of meaning.

A converts what they want to convey into signs such as words or diagrams (encoding) and sends them, and B interprets (reconstructs) them through their own knowledge and experience. As a result, a gap can arise between the sender's intention and the receiver's understanding.
Diagrams and facial expressions are merely supplementary, so as long as what one wants to convey is put into words and sent, no misunderstanding will arise.

questiontext.text: When the stance toward generative AI is expressed as "AI is a tool; judgment is your own," which of the following behaviors best aligns with this way of thinking?

generalfeedback.text: Generative AI is useful as a tool for drafting and brainstorming, but posing the questions, making judgments in light of the context, and taking responsibility for the results are the human's role, and the output must always be verified. A is wholesale delegation, C is an extreme of total rejection, and D is the error of uncritically prioritizing the AI.

answer.text: Leaving everything to generative AI, from setting the question of a report to its conclusion, and submitting the output as is

Using generative AI as a tool for drafting and brainstorming, while considering that posing the questions, judging things in context, and taking responsibility for the results are your own duty, and always verifying the output
Because generative AI can contain errors, avoiding using it at all for research or study
Because the output of generative AI is superior to that of humans, always adopting the AI's answer whenever it conflicts with your own thinking

questiontext.text: A Chiba University student is thinking, "Since drafting a report with generative AI was OK in Professor A's class, it must of course be OK in Professor B's class and for my graduation thesis too." Based on the "Guidelines on the Use of Generative AI in Education and Learning at Chiba University," select the two most appropriate responses.

generalfeedback.text: Under the guidelines, whether generative AI may be used for assignments and the like is in principle judged by the instructor in charge of each class (B). For research and the graduation thesis, an understanding of research ethics, keeping track of where AI was used, and responsibility for the results are essential, and there are also problems of incorrect references and code (C). A (decided uniformly) and D (the student decides freely) are incorrect.

answer.text: Because permission or prohibition is decided uniformly across the entire university, one may assume that the same treatment applies to any class or to the graduation thesis
Because whether generative AI may be used is in principle decided by the instructor in charge of each class, one should individually confirm the instructions and conditions of Professor B's class

Whether it can be used in research requires an understanding of research ethics; it is essential to keep track of where AI was used and to be able to take responsibility for the results, and there are also many problems such as producing incorrect reference lists or code
Whether it may be used is for the student themselves to decide freely, and there is no need to follow the instructor's instructions

questiontext.text: What does the saying often heard in data analysis, "correlation is not causation," mean? Choose the most appropriate option.

generalfeedback.text: Correlation does not imply causation. A third factor (a confounder) can affect both and produce a spurious correlation (e.g., ice cream sales and drowning accidents are confounded by "temperature"). Even if the correlation coefficient is high, the direction of cause and effect is not determined, and there are cases where no correlation appears even when causation exists.

answer.text: Even if two things are correlated (a relationship in which when one increases or decreases the other does too), there can be a "spurious correlation" due to a third factor (a confounder), and one is not necessarily the cause of the other
If there is a correlation, one is necessarily the cause of the other, so changing either one will necessarily change the result as well
The higher the correlation coefficient, the more certainly even the direction of which is cause and which is effect is determined
Between two things that have a causal relationship, a correlation never appears

questiontext.text:
The following figure represents the main components of a PC. [① ____: serves as the overall "brain," performing computation and control / ② Main memory: a working desk that the CPU reads from and writes to directly / ③ ____: specialized for massively parallel processing such as image rendering and AI training] Which combination is most appropriate for ① and ③?

* Fill in the blank marked "?" in the figure above.

generalfeedback.text: The CPU is the "brain" (computation and control), memory is the "working desk," and the GPU handles massively parallel processing. This figure-completion item asks whether you can identify the role of each component.

answer.text: ① CPU and ③ GPU
① GPU and ③ CPU
① SSD and ③ CPU
① Memory and ③ Motherboard

name.text: Q_記憶装置の階層_穴埋め (EN)

questiontext.text:
The following figure arranges a computer's memory hierarchy so that the higher levels are faster with smaller capacity and the lower levels are slower with larger capacity. [① Registers (inside the CPU) → ② ____ → ③ Main memory → ④ Secondary storage (HDD/SSD)] Which is most appropriate for ② — a form of storage that is faster than main memory and reduces the CPU's wait time by copying frequently used data close to the CPU?

* Fill in the blank marked "?" in the figure above.

generalfeedback.text: The memory hierarchy compensates for the trade-off between "fast but small" (registers, cache) and "slow but large" (main memory, secondary storage) by layering them. The answer for ② is cache memory.

answer.text: Cache memory
Virtual memory
Video memory
Cloud storage

questiontext.text: Which of the following is the most appropriate advantage of organizing storage devices into a hierarchy such as registers, cache, main memory, and secondary storage?

generalfeedback.text: By combining fast and expensive storage (registers and cache) with slow but cheap, large-capacity storage (main memory and secondary storage) into a hierarchy, and placing frequently used data in the upper levels, you can achieve both speed and capacity. The hierarchy does not equalize price and speed, make storage non-volatile, or automatically increase data.

answer.text: Because it combines fast but small-capacity storage with slow but large-capacity storage, achieving a good balance of both speed and capacity.
Because the more layers you add, the more all storage devices come to have the same speed and the same price.
Because dividing storage into layers prevents all data—including the data in main memory—from being lost even when the power is turned off.
Because the layering causes data to be automatically backed up without the CPU having to perform any computation.

questiontext.text: What is a 'hallucination' in generative AI? Which of the following is the most appropriate description?

generalfeedback.text: A hallucination is a phenomenon in which generative AI produces incorrect information, caused by errors, biases, or staleness (the cutoff) of the training data. Its output must be checked for accuracy and sources against reliable references. Option A describes a deepfake, Option C differs from the explanation of the cutoff and is incorrect, and Option D concerns prompting tips and is a separate issue.

answer.text: A fake video or image created intentionally with malicious intent (a deepfake).
A phenomenon in which generative AI produces plausible-sounding but incorrect information.
A feature that retrieves information dated after the cutoff (the most recent point) of the training data.
A technique of including the four elements of role, task, background, and format in a prompt.

questiontext.text: Which of the following best describes the relationship between an OS (operating system) and applications?

generalfeedback.text: The division of roles between the OS (the foundation that manages resources) and applications (tools that serve a purpose). Applications cannot run without an OS, and the same application will not run unchanged if the OS type differs (OS dependence). Think of it with examples such as Windows/macOS and Word/Chrome.

answer.text: Applications manage hardware and software resources, and the OS is a tool that serves a specific purpose on top of them.
The OS, as the "foundation," manages and controls resources (hardware and software), while applications serve specific purposes. Applications cannot run without an OS.
The OS and applications are the same thing, merely called by different names.
Applications run by using the OS's functions, but even if you replace the OS with a different type, the same application will run unchanged.

name.text: Q_大規模言語モデルの仕組み (EN)

questiontext.text: Which of the following best describes how a large language model (generative AI) such as ChatGPT produces text?

generalfeedback.text: Because the mechanism is statistical next-token prediction, plausible-sounding errors (hallucinations) can occur. Understanding this mechanism is a prerequisite for the appropriate use of, and precautions regarding, generative AI.

answer.text: It searches through a huge collection of question-and-answer pairs prepared in advance by humans that say "answer this question this way," and returns the matching answer.
Based on statistical probabilities learned from large amounts of text, it generates text by repeatedly predicting the "likely next word (token)" that follows the context.
Because it is constantly connected to the internet and searches for the correct answer in real time, it never gets facts wrong.
It understands the meaning of text the same way humans do, and answers only after judging for itself whether something is factual.

questiontext.text: Which of the following best describes the difference in characteristics between a CPU and a GPU?

generalfeedback.text: The GPU's "massively parallel" nature underpins the training and inference of generative AI. The CPU is a general-purpose brain and the GPU specializes in parallel processing, so they play different roles (the GPU is neither a superset nor dedicated solely to rendering).

answer.text: A CPU excels at massively parallel processing that performs huge numbers of simple calculations at once, while a GPU excels at performing complex processing one step at a time in sequence.
A GPU is a superset of a CPU, and can perform everything a CPU does, only faster.
A GPU is a device dedicated to rendering for screen display, and cannot be used for computations such as training AI.

A CPU is a general-purpose brain that handles complex processing and controls each device, while a GPU specializes in massively parallel processing for image rendering and simple calculations, making it well suited to 3D graphics and training AI.

name.text: Q_アナログのデジタル化_穴埋め (EN)

questiontext.text:
The following diagram shows the flow of digitizing analog information. [Analog signal → (1) sampling (taking values at fixed intervals) → (2) ____ (approximating the extracted values to predetermined discrete levels) → (3) encoding (converting into a sequence of 0s and 1s) → digital data]. Which of the following is the most appropriate term to fill in (2)?

* Fill in the blank marked "?" in the figure above.

generalfeedback.text: The three stages of analog-to-digital conversion (sampling, quantization, encoding). Step (2) is "quantization," which approximates the extracted values to discrete levels.

answer.text: Quantization
Encryption
Compression
Decryption

questiontext.text: When negative integers are represented using two's complement, which of the following expresses, in decimal, the range of values that can be represented with an 8-digit binary number? (Public exam question, IT Passport Examination, Spring 2012, Question 52)

generalfeedback.text: In two's complement representation, the most significant bit also serves as the sign, and there is only one representation of zero, so there is one more value on the negative side than on the positive side (asymmetric). With 8 digits, the range is -2^7 to 2^7-1, i.e., -128 to 127. This is the standard representation in today's computers.

questiontext.text: An n-bit string can distinguish 2ⁿ different states (2¹=2, 2²=4, 2³=8, 2⁴=16, 2⁵=32, 2⁶=64, 2⁷=128, 2⁸=256). If an experimental device has a total of 40 states that must be told apart, what is the minimum number of bits n needed to uniquely encode all 40 states?

generalfeedback.text: Find the smallest n satisfying 2ⁿ ≥ 40. 2⁵=32 is too few, while 2⁶=64 meets the condition, so n=6 (with 24 patterns left over). Option A is insufficient, C satisfies the condition but is not the minimum, and D confuses the number of states with the number of bits.

answer.text: 5 bits
6 bits
8 bits
40 bits

questiontext.text: When digitizing an image, the data size changes depending on how color (gradation) is represented, even for the same number of pixels. The number of bits per pixel is the number of bits needed to represent the gradation (n bits for 2ⁿ levels). What is the data size, in bytes, of an 8×8 = 64-pixel image represented as a 256-level grayscale image (1 pixel = 8 bits)?

generalfeedback.text: Since 256 levels = 2⁸, each pixel is 8 bits = 1 byte. 64 pixels × 1 byte = 64 bytes. Option A corresponds to simple binary (1 bit per pixel), B to 4 colors (2 bits), and D to RGB full color (24 bits).

answer.text: 8 bytes
16 bytes
64 bytes
192 bytes

questiontext.text: Which of the following is the most appropriate reason why it is convenient to digitize (represent as 0s and 1s) analog sound and images?

generalfeedback.text: Digitization turns information into a sequence of 0s and 1s, whose values are unlikely to be corrupted during copying and transmission (resistance to degradation), and lets sound, images, and text all be processed and integrated uniformly as the same 0s and 1s. Because sampling and quantization discard some information, it is not 'complete preservation,' nor is the data necessarily smaller or automatically corrected.

answer.text: Because the data resists degradation even after repeated copying and transmission, and different kinds of data can be processed and integrated together using the same method.
Because digitization always preserves the original analog information completely, without losing any of it.
Because digitization always makes the data size smaller than the original analog data.
Because once digitized, the content of the information is automatically corrected without any computation.

questiontext.text: Which of the following is the most appropriate reason why it is convenient for a computer to represent negative numbers using two's complement?

generalfeedback.text: With two's complement, 'A − B' can be executed using only an adder as 'A + (two's complement of B),' so no dedicated subtraction hardware is required (simpler circuitry). The representable range is determined by the number of bits and is not infinite; since this is an integer representation it has nothing to do with rounding errors, and the number of digits does not match decimal.

answer.text: Because subtraction can be computed with the same circuit as addition, so no separate dedicated subtraction circuit is needed.
Because using two's complement makes the range of representable numbers infinite.
Because using two's complement eliminates rounding errors in fractions entirely.
Because with two's complement, the same number of bits can represent numbers with as many digits as in decimal.

questiontext.text: In a relational database, instead of using one huge table as-is, “normalization”—a design that divides it appropriately into multiple tables—has which of the following as its main advantage? Choose the most appropriate one.

generalfeedback.text: The main purpose of normalization is to reduce duplication of the same information and to prevent inconsistencies (update anomalies) on updating (B). A is the opposite: normalization tends to increase joins and slow reads (for speed one deliberately denormalizes by keeping duplication). C is redundancy that increases duplication, the opposite of normalization. D is wrong because normalization actually requires joins—all realistic misconceptions.

answer.text: Because the more the tables are divided, the faster searches (reads) always become, so it is done to improve performance.
Because reducing duplication of the same information makes it easier to prevent inconsistencies that arise when, upon updating, only some copies are forgotten to be corrected.
To hold the same data redundantly by copying it across multiple tables, so that the data can be restored even if one table is damaged.
Because the tables become completely independent and there is no longer any need to join tables at all.

name.text: Q_サブネットマスクの役割 (EN)

questiontext.text: Which of the following correctly describes the role of a subnet mask? (Spring 2016 IT Passport Examination, publicly released question, Q70)

generalfeedback.text: A subnet mask separates an IP address into its network portion and its host portion. Option A describes NAT, B describes ARP, and D describes DNS, so these must not be confused. This concept underlies the determination of whether two hosts are on the same LAN (the AND operation).

answer.text: When relaying between the internet and an internal network, it maps global IP addresses to private IP addresses.
It determines the Ethernet MAC address that corresponds to an IP address.
It separates an IP address into the network address and the host address that identifies each individual computer belonging to that network.
It maps the domain name of a communication partner to its IP address.

questiontext.text: Which of the following is the most appropriate advantage of agreeing on common communication rules (protocols) worldwide?

generalfeedback.text: A protocol is a shared set of agreed-upon rules for communication. By defining them in common worldwide, devices can interconnect using the same procedure even when their makers or models differ (interoperability). Zero latency, automatic encryption, and reduction to a single device type are all incorrect.

answer.text: Because devices from different manufacturers or running different operating systems can communicate with one another by following the same procedure.
Because unifying protocols shortens the physical distance required for communication, reducing latency to zero.
Because adopting common rules automatically encrypts the content of communication, making eavesdropping impossible.
Because using the same rules worldwide means each country no longer needs to build its own devices, so the variety of devices is unified into a single type.

questiontext.text: Which of the following is the most appropriate advantage of designing a communication system (such as TCP/IP) as multiple layers?

generalfeedback.text: The advantage of layering is the separation of roles and independence between layers. Even if a lower layer (wired/wireless) is changed, the upper layer (applications) can be used as is, and each layer can be developed and replaced separately. Speed improvement, direct delivery, and automatic compression are irrelevant.

answer.text: Because changing the internals of one layer is unlikely to affect other layers, so each layer can be developed, improved, and replaced independently.
Because the more layers you add, the faster the communication speed always becomes.
Because dividing into layers allows data to reach the partner directly without passing through any intermediate devices.
Because layering automatically compresses the data being sent by a factor equal to the number of layers.

name.text: Q_パケット交換_なぜ便利 (EN)

questiontext.text: Which of the following is the most appropriate advantage of "packet switching," in which communication data is divided into small packets for transmission?

generalfeedback.text: In packet switching, data is sent in small pieces, so a single line can be shared by many communications, and when a fault occurs each packet can be rerouted along a different path (efficiency and fault tolerance). It does not encrypt the data, nor does it remove the need to specify a destination; monopolizing the line is rather a feature of circuit switching (the telephone network).

answer.text: Because a single line can be shared by many communications, and even if a fault occurs on part of a route, traffic can easily be rerouted along another path.
Because dividing data into packets always encrypts the content during transmission, making eavesdropping impossible.
Because dividing the data means it is automatically delivered only to the correct partner without specifying a destination.
Because in packet switching, a single pair of partners can monopolize the line throughout the entire communication.

questiontext.text: As devices around the world connect to the internet, the conventional IPv4 address (32 bits) has become insufficient. Which of the following most appropriately describes IPv6, which was introduced to address this?

generalfeedback.text: IPv4 uses 32 bits (about 4.3 billion addresses), and its exhaustion became a problem. IPv6 extends addresses to 128 bits, allowing unique addresses to be assigned to a virtually unlimited number of devices. It does not replace addresses with domain names, is not an encryption standard, and does not increase speed.

answer.text: It extends addresses to 128 bits, making it possible to assign a unique address to a virtually unlimited number of devices.
It abolishes IP addresses themselves, enabling communication using only domain names.
It is a new encryption standard created to prevent eavesdropping by encrypting the content of communication.
It keeps IPv4's 32 bits as they are and merely increases the communication speed sixfold.

questiontext.text: Which of the following is the most appropriate reason why it is convenient to use domain names and DNS to access websites and the like?

generalfeedback.text: DNS translates easy-to-remember domain names into IP addresses. People can specify sites by name, and even if the IP changes when a server is relocated, the same name can keep being used by updating the mapping. It has nothing to do with encryption, abolishing IP addresses, or reducing the number of routers traversed.

answer.text: Because people can specify sites by easy-to-remember names, and can keep using the same name even if the corresponding IP address changes.
Because using domain names encrypts the communication so it cannot be eavesdropped on.
Because using DNS makes IP addresses themselves unnecessary, allowing all IP addresses worldwide to be abolished.
Because using domain names reduces the number of routers the communication passes through to zero.

questiontext.text: At what point does copyright, the right of an author, come into existence? (FY2015 Autumn IT Passport Examination, public question, Q1)

generalfeedback.text: Copyright comes into existence simultaneously with creation, requiring no procedures such as registration (the principle of no formalities). This is an essential difference from industrial property rights such as patents, and it forms the basis for understanding why unauthorized use is a problem.

answer.text: When the work is registered with the Agency for Cultural Affairs
When the work is created
When the work is transferred to another person
When the work is reproduced

questiontext.text: Among the following explanations about quotation under copyright law, which one is incorrect?

generalfeedback.text: A lawful quotation requires that the original text be used without alteration, clearly distinguished, and its source explicitly indicated. 'Paraphrasing in your own words' is not a quotation (so B is incorrect). The quoted portion should be enclosed in quotation marks and use the original text as-is.

answer.text: The work must already have been made public.
Rather than using the original text as-is, it should be expressed in your own words.
Your own opinion is the 'principal' part and the quoted portion is 'subordinate.'
The purpose must be 'reporting,' 'criticism,' or 'research.'

questiontext.text: Someone is about to post, without permission, another person's photos and illustrations found online to write a blog post, thinking that 'anything on the internet can be used freely.' In light of the rules and norms that must be observed in the information society, which of the following is the most appropriate point to make?

generalfeedback.text: The idea that 'all information on the internet can be used freely / copyright need not be considered' is wrong. Images on the internet are also copyrighted; you should check the terms of use and license and obtain permission if necessary. Options A, C, and D are all misconceptions and inappropriate.

answer.text: Information and images published on the internet may be used freely without worrying about copyright.
Information and images on the internet also carry rights such as copyright and cannot necessarily be used freely, so you should check the terms of use and license and obtain permission as needed.
If you do not indicate the source at all, no one can tell whose work it is, so it does not constitute infringement.
As long as it is a personal blog and not commercial, any image may be used without permission.

questiontext.text: When you open a certain website, the 'Agree to all' button is displayed large and in a conspicuous color, while 'Reject' and 'Settings' are placed in small, hard-to-find spots. What is such a display called, and how should the user appropriately behave? Choose the most appropriate answer.

generalfeedback.text: Browsing history is stored by advertising companies via cookies and can become targeted advertising. A design that makes 'Agree' conspicuous and 'Reject' hard to find—a dark pattern—steers the user in one direction. Knowing the mechanism, pause for a moment and decide for yourself how to hand over your data. Options A, C, and D misuse the terminology.

answer.text: It is called universal design, and since it is equally considerate to everyone, you may agree without hesitation.
It is called a dark pattern, and you should notice the nudging, pause for a moment, and choose only after confirming the scope you are willing to permit.
It is called failover, a switching display shown during a malfunction, so you may simply close it.
It is called opt-in, a mechanism in which 'reject' is automatically selected even if you press nothing.

name.text: Q_情プラ法_匿名でも特定 (EN)

questiontext.text: Some people think, 'Since I'm anonymous, no one will know it's me,' even when they post defamatory remarks or write threats of crimes online using an anonymous account. Which of the following is the most appropriate reason why this thinking is mistaken?

generalfeedback.text: The Information Distribution Platform Act, which took effect in April 2025 (strengthening the former Provider Liability Limitation Act), obligates major SNS to speed up and make transparent the removal of content, and posters can be identified via sender information disclosure orders. Crime threats can lead to arrest for offenses such as obstruction of business. Even anonymously, one cannot escape legal liability. Options A, C, and D are baseless.

answer.text: Because the moment you agree to the SNS terms of use, everyone's real name is made public.
Because, under the Information Distribution Platform Act, mechanisms to identify posters—such as sender information disclosure orders—are in place.
Because anyone can instantly determine a poster's name and address without legal procedures, as long as they know the IP address of the device used for the post.
Because on free SNS, the real name entered at registration is always set to be automatically displayed on the profile.

questiontext.text: There is an access point configured with WPA2 encryption. When a PC connects through this access point to a web server on the Internet, which of the following is the appropriate range over which WPA2 encryption takes effect? (IT Passport Examination, Autumn 2016, public question No. 79)

generalfeedback.text: WPA2 encrypts only the wireless segment (between the PC and the access point). Do not mistakenly assume that protection extends to the wired segment beyond it; correctly delimit the scope to which the encryption applies. "

answer.text: From the PC to the web server
From the PC to the firewall
From the PC to the access point
From the access point to the web server

questiontext.text: Which of the following best describes the advantage of "two-factor authentication," which uses something additional to a password, such as sending a code to a smartphone?

generalfeedback.text: Two-factor authentication combines two pieces of evidence of different kinds, such as knowledge (a password), possession (a smartphone, etc.), or biometrics. Even if one is leaked, a login cannot be completed without the other, making it easier to prevent damage (defense in depth). "No password needed," "automatic encryption," and "doubled speed" are all incorrect.

answer.text: Even if the password is leaked, it is hard to break in without the other factor, so protection remains even when one factor is compromised
With two-factor authentication, you no longer need to remember a password at all
Using two factors automatically encrypts the communication so that it cannot be eavesdropped
With two-factor authentication, the access speed to the server doubles

questiontext.text: X wants to send Y an email using public-key cryptography that cannot be read by any third party and "can be read only by Y." X and Y each hold one pair consisting of their own public key and private key, and the public keys are published so that anyone can obtain them. Which of the following correctly states the combination of keys used for encryption and decryption, and also correctly states the reason a third party eavesdropping on the communication channel cannot read this email?

generalfeedback.text: For confidential communication, the recipient Y's key pair is used. X encrypts with Y's published public key, and the resulting ciphertext can be decrypted only with the paired Y's private key (which only Y holds). Option B "encrypts with one's own private key," which is actually a signature: anyone can decrypt it with the paired public key, so it provides no confidentiality. Option C uses the textbook ordering of encryption/decryption, but mistakes the key owners, so only X could decrypt and Y cannot read it. Option D is symmetric-key (shared-key) cryptography, a different scheme that suffers from the key-distribution problem.

answer.text: X encrypts with "Y's public key" and sends it, and Y decrypts with "Y's private key." An eavesdropper can obtain Y's public key, but only the paired Y's private key can decrypt text encrypted with it, and since only Y holds that key, the eavesdropper cannot read it.
X encrypts with "X's private key" and sends it, and Y decrypts with "X's public key." Since the eavesdropper does not hold X's private key, they cannot decrypt it and cannot read the message body.

X encrypts with "X's public key" and sends it, and Y decrypts with "X's private key." This follows the basic principle of public-key cryptography of encrypting with a public key and reverting with the paired private key, and since only X holds the private key, the eavesdropper cannot read it.

X and Y encrypt and decrypt using a single shared key agreed upon in advance. Since only the two of them know this shared key and it is not published, the eavesdropper does not know the key and cannot read it.

name.text: Q_踏み台_更新の社会的責任 (EN)

questiontext.text: Some people leave their OS and software unupdated, thinking, "My PC has no important data, and if I'm targeted, I'm the only one who suffers." Which of the following is the most appropriate reason that neglecting updates "is not merely one's own problem and can affect others and society as well"?

generalfeedback.text: A hijacked PC or IoT device can be exploited as a relay point (stepping stone) for DDoS attacks or spam distribution (at Chiba University in 2024, a public server was used as a stepping stone to send about 60,000 spam emails). Because a victim can in turn become a perpetrator, updating is a social responsibility and not merely "one's own problem" (correct answer B). Option A is the mistaken belief that the impact "does not reach others"; option C is the typical misconception that "newer versions are more dangerous, so it is safer not to update" (in reality, updates close known vulnerabilities); option D confuses the presence of data with infection.

answer.text: Even if you suffer damage from neglecting updates, the impact stays only within your own PC and never extends to others
A hijacked PC can be used as a "stepping stone," forced to serve as a relay point and complicit in harming others
Because newer versions of software harbor more unknown vulnerabilities, it is actually safer not to update
If you store no data, malware cannot infect the PC in the first place

questiontext.text: In an era when individual tools such as generative AI and cloud services keep changing one after another, which of the following is the most appropriate attitude to acquire as part of information literacy?

generalfeedback.text: Because individual tools are short-lived, it is more important to acquire "how to learn" itself than to memorize operations. Through methods such as trying things on a small scale, using good materials, and asking others, keep verifying the "why" and "how" with your own hands. Option A is rote memorization of procedures, C is leaving things to others, and D ignores differences in the effectiveness of learning strategies.

answer.text: If you perfectly memorize the operating procedures of a specific app, you will have no trouble even when the technology changes

Rather than the tools themselves, acquire "how to learn," and keep verifying the "why" and "how" with your own hands through methods such as trying things on a small scale, learning from good materials, and asking others
Leave new technologies to the experts, and just keep using only the tools you can use right now
Since everyone learns differently, don't worry about differences in effectiveness and just choose the easiest method
